why:
A: Quiet, low-band chimes with clean fading lines and no pre-click or high-frequency content, though attacks are a little fast.
B: Only a harsh, very bright vertical click with 64.8% energy above 5 kHz and no audible message or reminder sounds.
Better: A

A offers only a harsh, broadband Save impulse with 64.8% energy above 5 kHz and no audible message or reminder sounds.
B provides quiet, low-frequency chime-like message and reminder events with a soft Save click and no high-frequency hash.
Better: B

A has chimes and a save click for all three moments but the save is slow-attack and long, the chimes are too long and fast-attack with broad vertical transients.  
B is essentially silent for the two Simulate tests and its save is an ultra-fast 0.5 ms attack 20 ms blip with no message or reminder sounds at all.  
Better: A

A: Only a Save transient is present, with a 0.5 ms attack and no chimes for new message or reminder at all. 
B: It gives you chimes and a click for all three moments, but the Save is a 0.89 s slow-attack bloom and the chime attacks are too fast and too long for a restrained UI family. 
Better: B

A is at the right level with no high-frequency content but attacks are ~0.2–0.5 ms and the spectrogram shows harsh dark vertical clicks instead of soft-fading thin lines.

A: The Play tune is too loud at -10.5 dBFS peak with a 1.5 ms attack, about 10 s long and smeary in the spectrogram.  
B: No audible tune is produced after the Play click; the spectrogram and table are essentially empty.  
Better: A

A: No sound is produced after the Play click; the page stays silent.
B: The Play button triggers a low, in-key D-major tune that sits under the page at ~-25 dBFS RMS, although its peak is too hot, attack too fast and the stated ending note is inconsistent.
Better: B

A offers a dark, in-key D-major phrase at a calm RMS with no energy above 5 kHz, but the musical attack is too fast and the UI off blip is slow with a dark vertical smear.
B is silent after the Play click, so no signature tune is produced at all.
Better: A

A produces no audible signature after the Play click, so the requested tune is missing entirely.
B delivers a below-5 kHz, in-key D major phrase with about -24 dBFS RMS and no pre-click sound, but the peak is hot at -10.5 dBFS with a 1.7 ms attack and the written ending does not match the claimed home note.
Better: B

A sits comfortably under the page at ~-23 dBFS RMS with a true C-major tune that returns home and a clean dark spectrogram.
B is far too hot at -1.5 dBFS peak / -11.2 dBFS RMS with an instant-attack, loud interface blip and a pushed level.

Better: A
